components.function: one indivisible trade that sets maximum life to 1 and grants immunity to chaos damage

components.name: lethal_pool
components.function: the life pool whose depletion is death, reduced to a constant of 1 so any damage reaching it is fatal

components.name: energy_shield_pool
components.function: the buffer that absorbs damage before it can reach the lethal pool

components.name: damage_ordering_rule
components.function: routes damage to the buffer first and to the lethal pool only after the buffer is depleted, except for damage that bypasses the buffer

components.name: chaos_immunity
components.function: full immunity to chaos damage, the damage type that ignores the buffer

components.name: recharge_regulator
components.function: refills the buffer only during quiet time (a period with no damage taken) and restarts the delay whenever damage lands, so refill depends on the gaps between hits rather than on elapsed time

components.name: recovery_converters
components.function: turn life-based recovery (leech, regeneration, flask recovery) into buffer recovery because the life pool is only 1; unlike recharge it does not wait for quiet time

components.name: threshold_calculator
components.function: derives stun and ailment thresholds from life before the override to 1, so life modifiers still scale them

components.name: excluded_subsystems
components.function: mechanics that need a life pool and stop working, such as low-life effects, life flasks and life-cost skills

diagnosis: channel_tampering: the reward signal is driven directly instead of earned (psychostimulant transporter blockade, electrode self-stimulation, agent editing its own reward), so prediction can never cancel it
specification_gaming: the reward is honest about a proxy, and the learner maximizes the proxy while the intended goal is ignored
proxy_overoptimization: continued optimization past the point where proxy and goal agree; true performance degrades while measured reward climbs
incentive_sensitization: wanting grows with repetition while liking stays flat or falls; cues alone trigger strong pursuit
allostatic_shift: the set point moves; baseline without the hijacking input feels aversive, so behavior is maintained by escape from withdrawal
habit_lock_in: action selection becomes stimulus-driven and insensitive to outcome value or punishment
objective_collapse: a single hijacked objective crowds out all others; the behavioral repertoire narrows (abandoned goals in addiction, mode collapse and lost diversity in an over-optimized policy)
peer_amplification: parallel learners share exploits, so one discovered hack spreads across the population (shared hack boards among training agents; social spread of drug use)
engineered_exploitation: an external designer tunes reward schedules for engagement or revenue against the user's own goals (variable-ratio payouts, near-miss effects, infinite feeds, loot boxes)
